notes: Derived ABox edit for relation-property coverage (subproperty): has_paternal_grandfather ⊑ grandchild_of. Derivability likely: no text states Astyanax's grandfather as such (0 exact 'Astyanax's grandfather'; 5 co-occurrences of 'grandson of Priam' with Astyanax, about 1.5% of 'Astyanax AND son of Hector'), while both father links are stated often (evidence). Premise route: 'the father of Astyanax's father' goes through the premises' description. Worlds (Decisions 1): each lists the premise that gives way and the sibling and descent links that go with it, as in people-replace-0003; neither changes a fact about anyone outside the family chain (Andromache stays Astyanax's mother and Hector's wife, Hecuba stays Hector's mother, Nestor's own sons are unchanged). w2 also loses the Iliad's naming story (Astyanax, 'lord of the city', as son of Troy's defender), which is part of the premise itself. Over-determination: Hector's father is not entailed by other firm facts the model is sure to hold separately (his brothers' father is Priam only for full brothers, which w1 revises to half-brothers), so both premises can give way; lopsided worlds are kept (Decisions 4). Why Astyanax and not Telemachus: some later sources make Sisyphus the father of Odysseus, so 'Who was Odysseus's father?' would have two defensible answers (R1). Nestor: clearly false, a king of the same epic cycle; Agamemnon was rejected because making Hector his son would set him against his own father's army, a firm plot fact outside the chain. R2: no prompt names the answer. Near query (his mother) is not a premise and is unchanged in both worlds. Formal check (FINDINGS C2, E): q1's original 'no' rests on Astyanax's maternal grandfather being Eetion (now a stated bridge with a check); the worlds name the premise that gives way and say only that someone else takes its place, and who that is follows from the edit.
